title: GfK/NIQ UK Consumer Confidence Barometer — September 2026: the last consumer read whose fieldwork closed BEFORE the FOMC/CPI/BoE policy week
source: EST: nielseniq.com/global/en/news-center/2026/headline-score-up-three-points-to-14-in-august/, re-fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200) for this canonical write — the August-2026 barometer release lists the remaining 2026 press-release dates verbatim as 'September 25th, October 23rd, November 20th and December 18th'. CORROBORATED the same session by a SECOND NIQ primary carrying an independently-published copy of the same list: the July-2026 release (news-center/2026/consumer-confidence-up-six-points-to-17-in-july/, fetched direct 2026-09-15) prints 'August 21, September 25, October 23, November 20, December 18' — and its August 21 entry is now history, matching the August edition's actual publication date. Two NIQ pages published seven weeks apart agree on 2026-09-25. THE DATE DOES NOT FOLLOW THE PUBLISHER'S OWN RULE OF THUMB AND THE LIST WINS: nielseniq.com/global/en/landing-page/consumer-confidence-barometer/ (the Barometer's own landing page, fetched direct 2026-09-15) states 'The latest data is provided to subscribers on the third Friday of the month in most months, with a publication schedule available at the start of the year' — the third Friday of September 2026 is the 18th, and the scheduled date is the FOURTH Friday, the 25th. Anyone deriving this date from the third-Friday convention lands a week early; the publisher's own dated list is the key. Filed estimate on three counts, none of them date doubt: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has CB: for the US Conference Board and UMICH: for Michigan and no slot for GfK/NIQ, and the schedule is a note inside a press release rather than a standing release calendar. The release TIME (00:01 London / 19:01 ET the prior evening) is the barometer's standing convention and was NOT verifiable from any NIQ primary this session — three NIQ pages were read and none states a time; re-verify at close-out. Checked 2026-09-15
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-15 by this event's own never-assessed lane from the single proposal proposals/uk-consumer-confidence-2026-09-25.from-uk-retail-sales-2026-09-18.json (filed 2026-09-15, read in full first, now inert). WHAT THIS ENTRY IS ABOUT, IN ONE LINE: the September barometer's FIELDWORK CLOSES BEFORE THE POLICY WEEK, so it is a pre-FOMC/pre-CPI/pre-BoE snapshot published after all three — every September fieldwork window in the three-year primary sample ended on or before the 13th (2023: Sep 1-13; 2024: Aug 30-Sep 13; 2025: Sep 1-11), while fomc-2026-09-16, uk-cpi-2026-09-16 and boe-decision-2026-09-17 all land later. Any recap reading the 09-25 print as the consumer's response to that week is wrong; that response shows up in the October 23 edition. SECOND: it is the survey half of a measured disagreement the uk-retail-sales-2026-09-18 lane set up — BRC-KPMG called August 2026 the weakest till since October 2024 (total +0.7% y/y, non-food -0.8%) while this barometer printed its HIGHEST HEADLINE IN TWO YEARS (-14, up three, major purchases -7, best since December 2021). THIRD, the directional lean and its evidence: three of the four August-to-September changes in the 2022-2026 series are negative (-5, +4, -7, -2; mean -2.50) against an unconditional monthly mean of +0.55 over 49 changes, and the two negative years are exactly the two whose September fieldwork sat inside pre-Budget tax-rise speculation, with NIQ's own commentary naming it in 2025 ('confidence inevitably falls' ahead of anticipated November tax increases). uk-autumn-budget-2026-10-28 is 33 days after this print and its tax-rise speculation was live throughout the fieldwork window. A secondary aggregator (TradingEconomics, labelled secondary) carries consensus -17. Expected LOW on the same measured grounds as every UK sibling: symbols [], no UK-listed name in this book, no sterling- or rates-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this. This calendar tracks US consumer sentiment eighteen times over and until this file tracked NO UK consumer sentiment read at all.
